A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisVM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the relocated qualitative analysis and retained case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original caption-generation experiments, human and GPT evaluations, hallucination measurements, inference-budget scaling and self-training results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, comparator results, computational-cost measurements, a reward-model ablation and a controlled sentence-selection experiment.

M1.justification: The TD objective, sentence-value head and inference procedure in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v3 adds SigLIP as an alternative training reward component, including its use with LLaVA-OV, whereas v1 specifies CLIP.

E1.justification: The COCO data, LLaVA description prompts and seven visual-comprehension plus two hallucination benchmarks are retained. Changing 'eight' to 'nine' corrects the benchmark count already represented in v1. AMBER is introduced as an object-coverage metric; the additional model backbones do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds MCTS to the caption-quality and hallucination comparisons. Appendix C, Table 7 adds HADPO, POVID, CSR and VCD comparisons. Conversely, the CLIP-BoN(6) self-training comparator in v1 Table 3 is removed from the corresponding v3 Table 4.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation configurations using LLaVA-OV-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B and LLaVA-1.5-7B, object-coverage and GPU-hour measurements, and a controlled candidate-selection experiment with greedy continuation. The stated self-training budget changes from five epochs to three; this documents a setting revision without establishing whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds the CLIP-versus-SigLIP reward ablation in Table 3 and a quantitative test of subsequent hallucinations after selecting from identical candidate sentences in Table 5. It also adds computational-cost and object-coverage analyses. The original search-size analysis and qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.1 newly specifies that human-evaluation results are averaged across ten evaluators; v1 reports win rates without explaining cross-evaluator aggregation. This adds limited statistical reporting, without establishing increased experimental runs. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces human win rates against CLIP-PRM, BoN and greedy decoding from 66.0%, 63.5% and 74.0% to 62.4%, 60.2% and 75.8%. Substantial new results cover MCTS, additional backbones, reward ablation, controlled continuation and computational cost. Existing LLaVA self-training scores are retained despite the changed epoch description, so they do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation and TD objective in Equation 1 are unchanged, and no new theorem, proof or derivation appears. v3 omits the displayed standard CHAIR formulas without changing their underlying metric definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the central claims: long-term vision-value guidance improves captions, supports inference-time scaling and enables self-training. Additional backbone results strengthen supporting evidence, while correcting the benchmark count does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting object coverage to avoiding artificially favorable hallucination scores from short captions, MCTS computation to per-input search, and stronger rewards to VisVM's generality. The original long-term-value, attention and self-training explanations remain, without new substantive failure-condition analysis.

D1.justification: v3 documents MCTS expansion and iteration settings, model-specific reward choices, and ten-evaluator blind judging with a shared evaluation rubric. Core appendix training details remain, relocated from Appendix C to B. The explicit code/model availability statement and repository link in v1's abstract are removed; actual external availability cannot be inferred.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for VCD, AMBER and HADPO, while removing MMed-RAG, RULE and LLaVA-Critic. It also removes the related-work distinction concerning LLaVA-Critic's response-level scoring. The broader positioning around inference-time search and self-training remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 edits grammar, rewrites parts of the introduction and evaluation narrative, and reorganizes the appendices. The original qualitative analysis moves from Section 5 to Appendix D, while quantitative analysis becomes Section 4.3. Much of the method exposition and conclusion remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the GPU-cost chart and tables for reward ablation, controlled sentence selection and additional methods. Existing comparison tables expand with model blocks and a coverage column, and Figure 3 gains an MCTS comparison. The original Figure 4 becomes appendix Figure 5, while the nine case-study tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's single-backbone evaluation and qualitative mechanism evidence. Additional backbones, stronger comparators, controlled continuation, reward ablation and measured computational costs support generality, mechanism and practical efficiency more convincingly. Removing CLIP-BoN and the code-access statement, together with the unexplained epoch revision, weakens comparison completeness and reproducibility, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
